```{r loading-library}

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(here)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(patchwork)
library(kableExtra)
library(broom)
```

```{r reading-data}
#| include: false

airquality_data <- read_csv(here("data/air_quality.csv"))
```

```{r tidying-data}
#| include: false

airquality_data<- airquality_data |> 
  mutate(
    month = month(date, label = TRUE, abbr= TRUE),
    year = as.factor(year(date))
  )
```

## Problem Introduction

::: columns

::: {.column width="60%"}
- Air pollution is a major public health issue causing respiratory problems leading to increased hospital admissions
- We will explore data on air pollution levels and hospital admissions in 8 major cities across 2020–2025
- This presentation will examine how air pollution has affected hospital intakes in the most polluted cities in the years 2020-2025
:::

::: {.column width="40%"}
![Credit: Thoracic and Sleep Group](air-polution-illustration.png){width="100%"}
:::

:::

## Dataset Exploration

- The dataset contained daily air quality and healthcare observations from eight cities between 2020 and 2025. 

- Key variables included: `Air Quality Index (AQI)`, `PM2.5`, `PM10`, `NO2`, `O3`, `temperature`, `humidity`, `hospital admissions`, and `hospital capacity`. 

- Daily observations were aggregated into monthly summaries and then yearly summaries to reduce short-term fluctuations and improve trend interpretation.

## Methodology

The analysis was conducted using R and several packages from the `tidyverse` [@R-tidyverse] ecosystem for data cleaning, transformation, modelling, and visualisation. 

The following ibraries were used:

::: {style="font-size: 0.8em;"}

- `lubridate` [@R-lubridate] for date manipulation

- `ggplot2` [@R-ggplot2] for data visualisation

- `patchwork` [@R-patchwork] for combining multiple plots

- `kableExtra` [@R-kableExtra] for enhanced table formatting

- `broom` [@R-broom] for tidying regression outputs

- `here` [@R-here] for reproducible file paths

:::

## Regression

```{r classification-of-data}
# Step 2 — Club all daily data into monthly summaries

monthly_summary <- airquality_data |>

  group_by(city, year, month) |>

  summarise(
    avg_aqi = mean(aqi, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_pm25 = mean(pm2_5, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_pm10 = mean(pm10, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_no2 = mean(no2, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_o3 = mean(o3, na.rm = TRUE),

    avg_temperature =
      mean(temperature, na.rm = TRUE),

    avg_humidity =
      mean(humidity, na.rm = TRUE),

    total_hospital =
      sum(hospital_admissions, na.rm = TRUE),

    avg_hospital_capacity =
      mean(hospital_capacity, na.rm = TRUE),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Step 3 — Club all months into yearly summaries

yearly_summary <- monthly_summary |>

  group_by(city, year) |>
    summarise(
    avg_aqi = mean(avg_aqi, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_pm25 = mean(avg_pm25, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_pm10 = mean(avg_pm10, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_no2 = mean(avg_no2, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_o3 = mean(avg_o3, na.rm = TRUE),

    avg_temperature =
      mean(avg_temperature, na.rm = TRUE),

    avg_humidity =
      mean(avg_humidity, na.rm = TRUE),

    yearly_total_hospital =
      sum(total_hospital, na.rm = TRUE),

    avg_hospital_capacity =
      mean(avg_hospital_capacity, na.rm = TRUE),

    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r top-3-polluted-cities}
# step 3
top3_polluted_cities <- yearly_summary |>

  filter(
    year %in%
      c("2020", "2021", "2022",
        "2023", "2024", "2025")
  ) |>

  group_by(city) |>

  summarise(
    overall_avg_aqi =
      mean(avg_aqi, na.rm = TRUE),

    overall_total_hospital =
      sum(yearly_total_hospital,
          na.rm = TRUE),

    overall_avg_capacity =
      mean(avg_hospital_capacity,
           na.rm = TRUE),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>

  arrange(
    desc(overall_avg_aqi)
  ) |>

  slice_head(n = 3)
```

```{r 3-least-polluted-cities}
least3_polluted_cities <- yearly_summary |>

  filter(
    year %in%
      c("2020", "2021", "2022",
        "2023", "2024", "2025")
  ) |>

  group_by(city) |>

  summarise(

    overall_avg_aqi =
      mean(avg_aqi, na.rm = TRUE),

    overall_total_hospital =
      sum(yearly_total_hospital,
          na.rm = TRUE),

    overall_avg_capacity =
      mean(avg_hospital_capacity,
           na.rm = TRUE),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>

  arrange(
    overall_avg_aqi
  ) |>

  slice_head(n = 3)
```

```{r Model-PM25-HospitalAdmission-Correlation}
#| echo: false
#| include: false
correlation_model <-lm(hospital_admissions ~ aqi + pm2_5 + pm10 + no2 + o3,
data = airquality_data)

summary(correlation_model)
```

::: columns

::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r regression-table}
#| fig-pos: "H"
#| label: "tbl-regression-results"
#| tbl-cap: "Linear Regression Results for Hospital Admissions"
tidy(correlation_model) |>

  rename(
    Variable = term,
    Coefficient = estimate,
    `Standard Error` = std.error,
    `t value` = statistic,
    `p value` = p.value
  ) |>

  kable(
    digits = 4
  ) |>

  kable_styling(
    font_size = 22
  ) |>

  row_spec(
    0,
    bold = TRUE,
    background = "#4682B4",
    color = "white"
  )
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r correlation-plot}
#| fig-pos: "H"
#| label: "fig-pm25-scatter"
#| fig-cap: "Correlation between Pollutants and Hospital Admissions"

ggplot(airquality_data, aes(x = pm2_5, y = hospital_admissions)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, color = "#4682B4") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "red") +
  labs(
    title = "Correlation between Pollutants and Hospital Admissions",
    subtitle = "PM2.5 is the only statistically significant predictor (p < 0.05)",
    x = "PM2.5",
    y = "Hospital Admissions"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
:::

:::

The regression analysis revealed that `PM2.5` levels were significantly positively associated with `hospital admissions` (p < 0.05), while other pollutants did not show a statistically significant relationship.

## Results

```{r comparison-plot}
#| label: "fig-pollution-hospital-comparison"
#| fig-cap: "Comparison of Pollution and Hospital Admissions Between the 3 Most Vs 3 Least Polluted Cities (2020–2025)"


comparison_yearly_data <- yearly_summary |>

  filter(
    city %in% c(
      top3_polluted_cities$city,
      least3_polluted_cities$city
    ),

    year %in%
      c("2020", "2021", "2022",
        "2023", "2024", "2025")
  )

comparison_yearly_data <- comparison_yearly_data |>

  mutate(
    pollution_group = case_when(

      city %in% top3_polluted_cities$city
        ~ "3 Most Polluted",

      city %in% least3_polluted_cities$city
        ~ "3 Least Polluted"
    )
  )

# PM2.5 trend plot

plot1 <- ggplot(
  comparison_yearly_data,

  aes(
    x = year,
    y = avg_pm25,
    color = city,
    linetype = pollution_group,
    group = city
  )
) +

  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +

  labs(
    title = "PM2.5 Trends by City",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Average PM2.5",
    color = "City",
    linetype = "Pollution Category"
) +

  theme_minimal()

# Hospital admissions trend plot

plot2 <- ggplot(
  comparison_yearly_data,

  aes(
    x = year,
    y = yearly_total_hospital,
    color = city,
    linetype = pollution_group,
    group = city
  )
) +

  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +

  labs(
  title = "Hospital Admissions by City",
  x = "Year",
  y = "Yearly Total Hospital Admissions",
  color = "City",
  linetype = "Pollution Category"
) +

  theme_minimal()

# Combine plots with shared legend

(plot1 / plot2) +

  plot_layout(guides = "collect") +

  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.box = "vertical"
  )
```
